column2: On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Part of the excellence of a person's Islam is his leaving what does not concern him.” A ḥasan hadith, reported by al-Tirmidhī and others in this way.

Min (“part of”): partitive or explanatory. Al-marʾ (“a person”): an individual. Mā lā yaʿnīhi (“what does not concern him”): what is of no importance to him in matters of religion and worldly life. Min ḥusni (“part of the excellence”): ḥusn (excellence) is the opposite of ugliness.
A Muslim should leave the meddling that does not concern him, whether in words, deeds or thoughts.
A person should busy himself with what concerns him, in which there is benefit for him in his religion or worldly life.
Whoever busies himself with what does not concern him is deficient in faith.

This hadith teaches us that whoever does not leave what does not concern him is weak in faith, and that part of the perfection of a servant's faith is his leaving the words and deeds that are of no importance to him and are not among his interests and affairs. A person should therefore concern himself with the matters that relate to his life, his means of livelihood and his happiness in the Hereafter,
and that is easy for whomever Allah makes it easy and grants success. When a person confines himself to what concerns him, he is safe from the consequences of what does not concern him,
and in safety there is much good.
A point of benefit: Luqmān was asked, “What brought you to what we see?”—meaning his excellence. He said: “Truthful speech, fulfilling the trust, and leaving what does not concern me.”
Over your mouth, against what does not concern you, / lock a firm lock, as far as you are able.
